question: How does one reach the supreme divine Person?
premises: One is endowed with yoga of practice
The mind does not go elsewhere
One reaches the supreme divine Person
O Partha, by thinking of him
After the breaking of the body
Freed from pain caused by the body
Afterwards one thinks of the Lord
inference: Disciplined practice and a one-pointed mind lead to the supreme divine Person, with final remembrance of the Lord after bodily death.
uncertainties: The supplied gloss after the verse may be commentary rather than mūla
Its exact syntactic relation to the verse is not fully clear
plain_english: By yoga of practice, with a mind that does not wander elsewhere, one reaches the supreme divine Person, O Partha, by thinking of him; after the body breaks, freed from bodily pain, one then thinks of the Lord.
